newsitem.title: USA: Mo. Senate OKs bill to cut state food sales tax.
newsitem.headline: Mo. Senate OKs bill to cut state food sales tax.

text.p: The Missouri Senate Thursday approved a bill to cut two percent from the state's general food sales tax, an aide to the bill's sponsor said.

Senators voted 30-0 to reduce the state's general sales tax on food and to phase in tax breaks for non-governmental pensioners as well as increasing income tax deductions for dependent children, said Ray Schneider, an aide to Sen. James Mathewson, D-Sedalia.
The Missouri House in late February approved a bill eliminating all three percent of the general state sales tax on food, a $230 million revenue reduction, according to state projections.
Neither version affects local sales taxes on food, which vary throughout Missouri, Schneider noted.
Missouri Gov. Mel Carnahan proposed eliminating the tax as part of his fiscal 1998 budget strategy to deal with a budget surplus that exceeds limits imposed by the state constitution.
Carnahan supports eliminating the tax and also many of the elements included in the Senate version of the bill, spokesman Chris Sifford said.
The two bills will be sent to a conference committee next week, Sifford added.
